paper.title_en: The investigation of various gravitational soliton profiles for Einstein’s vacuum field equations under the unified Hirota bilinear approach
paper.abstract_en: Einstein’s vacuum field equation (EVFE) occupies a central position in general relativity, governing the geometry of spacetime in regions free from matter sources. The nonlinear PDE analyzed here is a specific (1+1)-dimensional reduction of the full vacuum field equations, obtained by imposing the Guilfoyle metric ansatz and setting <math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e3328"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>; all results pertain to this reduced model. Despite its physical importance, the catalogue of exact nonlinear wave solutions for this reduced EVFE does not yet include spatially localized multi-component and breather-type structures: no such solutions have been constructed for this equation prior to this work. We address this gap by applying the Hirota bilinear method with strategically chosen polynomial test functions to obtain, within a single unified framework, an extensive family of exact analytic solutions: lump, lump 1-stripe, lump 2-stripe, lump-periodic, manifold periodic, rogue wave, Ma breather, Kuznetsov–Ma breather, generalized breather, Akhmediev breather, and the corresponding standard rogue wave. We further construct interaction solutions among lump, periodic, and kink-wave components and illustrate their three-scale spatial structure through contour analysis. Three-dimensional surface profiles and contour maps are generated for each solution class with systematic parameter variation, revealing how background level, wavenumber, and velocity parameters control the localization geometry, peak amplitude, and propagation direction. The solutions carry direct relevance to gravitational wave physics, nonlinear optics, and ocean wave dynamics, and provide benchmark configurations for numerical relativity and wave-scattering studies.
